issuing_body: National Technical Committee 260 on Cybersecurity of SAC (TC260)
covered_actors: Agentic AI developers, providers, and users
Open-source model providers and open-source communities
Government departments and sectoral competent/regulatory authorities
Industry organizations, social organizations, and research institutions
prohibited_practices: Sharing unique identity identifiers among agentic AI application instances
Invoking publicly known malicious tools by agentic AI systems
Using AI products or services to interfere in the internal affairs, social systems, or social order of other countries, or coercing other countries to take sides
Using AI in high-risk scenarios such as the manufacture of nuclear, biological, chemical, and missile weapons
Prohibited actions for downloading and using open-source models to be explicitly defined by open-source model providers and communities
implementation_notes: Bilingual (Chinese and English) Version 3.0 technical governance framework issued by TC260 under the guidance of the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC), updating Versions 1.0 (2024) and 2.0 (2025). As a non-binding standards framework, it establishes no direct statutory penalties, though Section 4.3.3 notes that illegal acts endangering national security, infringing personal rights, causing major harm, or committed intentionally are not exempted from legal liability under proposed regulatory sandboxes. It provides risk classifications (inherent, application, and secondary/derivative risks), technological countermeasures, comprehensive governance measures (including registration/filing for AI systems in critical information infrastructure and at least 6-month operational log retention in Section 5.3.6), role-based safety guidelines, and three appendices: 5-tier AI safety risk grading principles (Appendix 1), a full-lifecycle Agentic AI Risk Management Framework (Appendix 2), and Fundamental Principles for Trustworthy AI (Appendix 3).
